chapter: Teaching, the 1951 Big Show and New York nights
title: Strayhorn's lost arrangement of 'Unforgettable'
summary: Strayhorn wrote a great arrangement of Unforgettable for Nat, but its baritone part went missing and could never be duplicated; Collins and Willard speculate who took it.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Yeah. But few people were aware of the fact that he played guitar. I'm sure everybody in the band knew, you know, but that was a great band. Now Nat had a hit at that time, 'Unforgettable.' This was a big hit for him. But he wanted Billy Strayhorn to do an arrangement for him so he commissioned Billy to do another arrangement on 'Unforgettable' and that was the greatest arrangement of 'Unforgettable' I've ever heard. It was just -- now, when we left the show, someone took the baritone part. The arrangement never sounded the same, we could never get anyone to write the baritone part over, we -- I don't know whether Duke took it or --
Well, I heard that Tizol took it. I don't know.
Well, it would be more than Duke wouldn't want because he wanted somebody else to --
That's right, we could never duplicate --
Because he wouldn't want anyone else to
-- (inaudible) because he said he achieve success with any thing he felt was his felt was his and he felt Strayhorn was it.

This was the greatest arrangement of 'Unforgettable.' Nat just loved it. We could never --- they took one part, baritone part, and that was the arrangement. And we could never pin --- Strayhorn didn't have the -- what -- you know, he didn't have his master chart with him, you know, he didn't have the chart, so he couldn't write, he
couldn't duplicate it himself. And so we could never use that arrangement any more. It was very frustrating. We had guys in New York to try to duplicate it, write this baritone part. Nobody could.
But I heard that Tizol took it, but you said it was probably Duke.
MS. WILLARD: I don't know, depending on what was going on. But possibly Duke commissioned Tizol to take it, because Tizol could be as devious as Duke sometimes.
